title: Refit a wardrobe rail under the hat shelf, between a closed and an open end support
instruction: Fit the wardrobe rail into its two end supports.
context: Wardrobe rails hang a few centimetres under the hat shelf, between a closed end support on one side panel and an open U support on the other, so they are seen and reached only from below. The rail is cut a few millimetres short of the gap but is still too long to go in square, and the shelf leaves no room to tilt it up: the end is fed into the closed support with the rail swung out toward the front, then swung back and lowered into the U. People do this whenever a rail is taken out to clear a wardrobe or has been knocked out of its supports.
setup: Positions in cm from the arm-base line (x forward) and the midline (y left), one fixed layout matching the screenshot. Wardrobe section, fixed to the table: white melamine particleboard, base board 20 x 63.6 x 1.8 cm and two side panels 20 cm deep, 1.8 cm thick, 16 cm tall, inner faces 60.0 cm apart, both from x 22 to 42, centred on the midline. Hat shelf: the same board, 1.8 cm thick, between the panels from x 29.0 to 42 (covering the rail and both supports from above), its underside 14.75 cm above the table (5.5 cm above the rail's top). Left panel (y +30): a closed chrome end support, a 2.9 x 2.9 cm bore 1.0 cm deep, axis 8.0 cm above the table at x 32. Right panel (y -30): an open chrome U support at the same axis, 2.9 cm wide inside, 1.5 cm deep from the panel, floor 6.75 cm above the table, cheeks 2 cm tall, open on top. Rail: a round chrome steel wardrobe rod 2.5 cm across, 59.2 cm long, 0.35 kg, lying left-right in two grooved blue foam blocks (6 x 6 x 5 cm), the blocks centred at x 16, y +10 and y -10, the rail centred on the midline at x 16.
scoring: Final state only, with both grippers open and at least 3 cm from the rail and the rail still (moving under 1 mm) for the last 1 s; otherwise 0. 0.4 if the left end is at least 0.8 cm into the closed support's bore. 0.4 if the right end rests on the U support's floor (end centre within 0.3 cm of the support axis height, at least 0.5 cm over the floor). 0.2 more if both ends are in and the rail is level within 1 degree. Full score 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the rail's right end out of the U, slide the left end out of the closed support, and lay the rail back on the foam blocks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes and cylinders. The rod is a 25 mm cylinder; the closed support is a square 29 mm bore 1.0 cm deep and the U is 29 mm wide. The wardrobe section with its hat shelf is one fixed 25 kg part; the grooved foam blocks are one 3 kg part. Friction 1.2 everywhere. No screws or fixings.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the rail is never lifted out of the foam blocks); demo: 1.0
